teacherTips.leadin: 课堂上可先请1–2位学生口头分享，用2分钟左右快速导入话题，营造"听故事"的课堂氛围，再进入下一环节。自学模式下学生可直接写下自己的想法。
teacherTips.debate: 可先让学生个人表态，再按立场分组做小型辩论，2分钟准备后各组陈述理由。下面的呼应形式对比可作为辩论后的收束追问。
teacherTips.exit: 可作为下课前的快速检验：请学生用今天学到的一个生词造句，教师快速抽查2–3位。

passageParagraphs: Storytelling plays a big part in the childhood of most people growing up on the Caribbean Islands. It is a tradition that was brought over from Africa by their ancestors many years ago and is a way of keeping their shared culture alive. The stories are a way of remembering the past and making sure it's not forgotten in the future.

And despite the modern distractions of television and video games, many Caribbean families still gather on the steps outside their homes, with the full moon in the sky and the wind blowing gently through the palm trees, to hear stories that they have already heard many times before.

The storyteller has an important position in Caribbean society. But it is not an art that is learned quickly. Good storytellers take years to perfect their performances. First, they must collect a catalogue of good stories, which are often short and simple and should work well for people of all ages. They must then practise these on family members to test out their material before moving on to larger crowds in local community centres. From there they may choose to become travelling storytellers and move from town to town looking for new audiences to share their tales with. And the very best storytellers make it onto the international stage and travel the world. More recently many storytellers have started using film to reach even more people.

With many Caribbean islands and people originating from many African countries, there are lots of types of stories to be told. One common feature though is the performance tradition known as 'crick crack'. Although this may differ a little in each country, the basic idea is that the audience participates in the storytelling. For example, in St Lucia, where stories are usually told in French, the storyteller (known as the 'conteur') announces that he or she wants to tell a story by shouting out 'Crick!' and the audience show they want to listen by responding 'Crack!' Throughout the performance, the storyteller continues to involve the audience by inviting them to answer questions and riddles and to make comments. In this way, the storyteller and the audience become an almost equally important part of the whole experience.

But as well as the many traditional tales and myths there are to be told, storytellers also create their own characters, and the most successful of these have become part of cultural life. One of the most famous storytellers in the West Indies is Paul Keens-Douglas, who was born in Trinidad but grew up in Grenada. Probably his most popular character, Tanti Merle, is known throughout the region and appears in many of his stories. Tanti Merle is a woman who is not afraid to say what she thinks and Keens-Douglas uses her as a lovable comic figure to make comments on everyday life in the Caribbean.

gist.hint: 先限时1–2分钟快速通读全文，不逐词读，抓住大意。
gist.question: What is the main idea of this article?
options: Caribbean storytelling is a dying tradition that young people are no longer interested in.
Storytelling is a living tradition in Caribbean culture, passed down through generations and shaped by unique performance styles.
Storytellers in the Caribbean only perform for tourists as entertainment.
Caribbean stories are always written down rather than spoken aloud.

gist.doneMessage: ✓ 结构梳理完成——这是一篇"总起-分述-举例收束"的说明文。

structure.question: How is this article organised overall? (Hint: it is not a single chronological sequence.)
structure.summaryHtml: 全文整体是Description（分说式）结构——围绕"讲故事传统"从5个方面展开；其中第3段内部单独构成一个Sequence（顺序）子结构，讲述说书人从家庭到国际舞台的成长路径。
structure.questionZh: 全文整体如何组织？（提示：并非单一时间顺序）

questions.question: Where did Caribbean storytelling come from, and what two jobs does it do for the community?
questions.answerEn: It was brought from Africa by ancestors. Stories help people remember the past and keep their shared culture alive for the future.
questions.answerZh: 传统由祖先从非洲带来。故事帮助人们记住过去，并让共同的文化在未来继续流传。
questions.questionZh: 加勒比讲故事传统来自哪里？它对社群有哪两件“工作”？

questions.question: How is this opening paragraph organised — what comes first, and what follows?
questions.answerEn: It opens with a broad claim (storytelling matters in Caribbean childhood), then adds origin (Africa) and purpose (memory + culture). Logic: origin + function.
questions.answerZh: 先下结论（讲故事在童年中很重要），再补充起源（非洲）与功能（记忆与文化）。段内逻辑是「起源 + 功能」。
questions.questionZh: 开篇段落如何组织——先写什么，后写什么？

questions.question: In “keeping their shared culture alive”, what does “alive” suggest about culture?
questions.answerEn: “Alive” treats culture as something that can fade or die unless people actively sustain it through stories — not a static museum piece.
questions.answerZh: alive 把文化看作若不主动维系就会消亡的东西——不是博物馆里的静态展品。
questions.questionZh: 在 “keeping their shared culture alive” 中，alive 暗示文化怎样？

questions.question: What modern distractions does the writer name, and where do families still gather to hear stories?
questions.answerEn: Television and video games. Families still gather on the steps outside their homes, under the full moon with wind in the palm trees.
questions.answerZh: 电视与电子游戏。家庭仍在屋外台阶上聚会，月圆之夜，风吹棕榈。
questions.questionZh: 作者点名了哪些现代干扰？家庭仍在哪里听故事？

questions.question: How does the “despite… still…” pattern shape the paragraph’s argument?
questions.answerEn: It concedes modern entertainment first, then stresses that the outdoor storytelling ritual continues anyway — contrast that highlights resilience.
questions.answerZh: 先承认现代娱乐的存在，再强调户外讲故事仪式依然延续——用让步突出传统的韧性。
questions.questionZh: “despite… still…” 句式如何塑造本段论点？

questions.question: What mood does the night-time outdoor scene create, and why might the writer choose that imagery?
questions.answerEn: Warm, communal, almost timeless. Moonlight and palm trees make the tradition feel rooted in place and atmosphere, not just a habit that competes with screens.
questions.answerZh: 温暖、社群、近乎永恒。月光与棕榈让传统扎根于地方与氛围，而不只是与屏幕竞争的习惯。
questions.questionZh: 夜户外场景营造了什么氛围？作者为何选用这些意象？

questions.question: List the main stages on the path from beginner to international storyteller.
questions.answerEn: Collect a catalogue of short, simple stories → practise on family → perform in community centres → travel town to town → the best reach the international stage (and some use film).
questions.answerZh: 积累短小故事库 → 在家人面前练习 → 社区中心演出 → 城镇巡回 → 最优秀者登上国际舞台（也有人用电影扩大受众）。
questions.questionZh: 列出从初学者到国际说书人的主要阶段。

questions.question: What organisational pattern does this paragraph use that other paragraphs do not?
questions.answerEn: A clear Sequence / process: skills and stages widen step by step. It is the article’s only full chronological career path.
questions.answerZh: 清晰的 Sequence（顺序）结构：技艺与舞台逐步扩大。这是全文唯一完整的生涯时间线段落。
questions.questionZh: 本段使用了其他段落没有的哪种组织模式？

questions.question: Why must storytellers test material on family before larger crowds?
questions.answerEn: Family is a safe rehearsal space: short stories for all ages need feedback before community or travelling audiences — craft is refined before stakes rise.
questions.answerZh: 家人是安全的试演场：面向各年龄的短故事需要反馈；技艺先打磨，再提高舞台风险。
questions.questionZh: 为何必须先在家人面前试演，再到更大人群？

questions.question: In the “crick crack” tradition, what does the storyteller shout, and how does the audience reply?
questions.answerEn: The storyteller shouts “Crick!”; the audience answers “Crack!” to show they want to listen. The audience also answers questions, riddles, and comments throughout.
questions.answerZh: 说书人喊 “Crick!”，听众回 “Crack!” 表示想听。表演中听众还会答题、猜谜、发表评论。
questions.questionZh: 在 “crick crack” 传统中，说书人喊什么？听众如何回应？

questions.question: Why does the writer say storyteller and audience become “almost equally important”?
questions.answerEn: Performance is co-created: without the call-and-response and ongoing participation, the ritual (and the experience) would collapse into a one-way lecture.
questions.answerZh: 表演是共同完成的：没有一呼一应与持续参与，仪式就会变成单向讲述。
questions.questionZh: 作者为何说说书人与听众变得“几乎同等重要”？

questions.question: Paul Keens-Douglas uses Tanti Merle to comment on everyday Caribbean life. Do you think comedy is a strong way to discuss social issues? Why or why not?
questions.answerEn: Open response — strong answers note that a lovable comic figure can lower defences, reach wide audiences, and still critique daily life; weaker answers ignore the social-comment function.
questions.answerZh: 开放性思考——有力回答会指出可爱的喜剧角色能降低防备、扩大受众，同时评论日常生活；较弱回答会忽略社会评论功能。
questions.questionZh: Paul Keens-Douglas 用 Tanti Merle 评论加勒比日常生活。你认为喜剧是讨论社会议题的有力方式吗？为什么？

deepDive.title: Four Threads Through the Text
deepDive.subtitle: 贯穿全文的四条线索
deepDive.question: What four themes does the writer weave through the whole article — not just three "big ideas"?
bulletsEn: storytelling was brought from Africa and keeps shared culture alive across generations.
despite modern distractions, families still gather to hear familiar tales outdoors.
becoming a storyteller takes years — building a catalogue, testing on family, then reaching wider audiences.
crick-crack rituals and characters like Tanti Merle show the tradition still evolves with its audience.
deepDive.summaryEn: The article is organised as a description of a living tradition — heritage, resilience, craft, and performance all interlock.
bulletsZh: 讲故事传统源自非洲，帮助几代人保持共同文化活力。
尽管有电视和游戏等干扰，家庭依然在户外聆听熟悉的故事。
成为说书人需多年磨练——积累故事库、家人试演，再走向更广阔的舞台。
"克里克-克拉克"仪式与 Tanti Merle 等角色说明传统仍在与听众共同演变。
deepDive.summaryZh: 全文以分说方式描绘一项活态传统——传承、韧性、技艺与表演彼此交织。
deepDive.questionZh: 作者在全文编织了哪四条线索——而不只是三个“大观点”？

powerWords.meaningZh: 地位；社会角色（不是物理上的“位置”）

powerWords.meaningEn: to refine a skill over time, not "flawless"
powerWords.meaningZh: （动词）打磨、精进技艺（不是形容词“完美的”）

powerWords.meaningEn: a curated collection built up deliberately
powerWords.meaningZh: 有意积累的目录 / 汇编（此处指故事库）

powerWords.meaningEn: takes an active part; stresses co-creation, not passive listening
powerWords.meaningZh: 参与；强调主动共创，而非被动听讲

powerWords.meaningEn: charming enough to carry social commentary
powerWords.meaningZh: 讨人喜爱的——足以承载对社会生活的评论

phrases.meaningEn: sustain a tradition so it does not die out
phrases.meaningZh: 让某事物保持活力；维系传统不致消亡

phrases.meaningEn: require a long time to master — stresses long apprenticeship
phrases.meaningZh: 需要多年才能做成——强调长期磨练

phrases.word: make it onto the international stage
phrases.meaningZh: 登上国际舞台；获得世界范围的认可

trueFalse.text: Children in the Caribbean don't use modern technology.
trueFalse.reason: The article says families still gather to hear stories “despite the modern distractions of television and video games” — implying they do use them.

trueFalse.text: Storytellers have to learn long detailed stories.
trueFalse.reason: The article says storytellers collect stories “which are often short and simple.”

trueFalse.text: Audiences play an important part in the storytelling.
trueFalse.reason: “The audience participates in the storytelling” and becomes “almost equally important” as the storyteller.

trueFalse.text: You should shout 'crack' if you want to hear a story.
trueFalse.reason: The audience responds ‘Crack!’ to show they want to listen.
The article says storytellers also “create their own characters,” like Paul Keens-Douglas's Tanti Merle.
